thesis: ViTrox has spectacular reported demand growth, but the bear establishes an unfavorable valuation/conversion combination at 93.83x trailing and estimated 55.86x forward earnings. H1 CFO fell to RM24.163m despite surging profit, leaving negative RM15.766m FCF and larger inventories/receivables. Net cash protects execution feasibility more directly than shareholder returns from a compressed growth premium.
strongest_counterexample: Q2 revenue grew 104.8% and profit 202.3%, while RM286.722m net cash excluding leases gives the company a real buffer to convert working capital into collected earnings without immediate borrowing.
invalidation_conditions: Comparable H1 CFO above the prior RM74.190m and positive FCF, with receivables no higher than RM527.137m, would weaken the cash-conversion basis for sell.

A later comparable period delivering positive FCF and year-on-year revenue growth above the present 104.8% quarterly rate would require reassessing whether earnings growth is catching up with the premium.
decisive_factors: Cash conversion deteriorated rather than merely lacking future certainty.
Tax incentives qualify profit recurrence; overbought technicals add timing risk without proving reversal.
